title: VPC & On‑Prem Benchmark Orchestrator for Customer‑Environment Emulation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an orchestrator that can spin up deterministic, customer‑environment emulations for Private (VPC/on‑prem) benchmarking. The goal is to enable reproducible runs that mirror a customer’s topology, traffic mix, and model/quantization configuration so we can measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, tail behavior, and detect regressions across runtime changes. This is focused on enabling engineering + solutions teams to: 1) reproduce customer‑reported perf issues in-house, 2) run pre‑flight benchmarks for Private upgrades, and 3) maintain a historical benchmark store optimized for automated regression detection.
motivation: Customers frequently surface performance issues that only appear in their private topologies (network egress restrictions, custom KV cache sizes, atypical request size distributions). Current harnesses reproduce traffic but lack a compact orchestrator that composes environment snapshots, load profiles, model variants, and compares runs against golden baselines with automated alerts. This project reduces time-to-debug and protects release quality for Private deployments.
scope: MVP: (a) environment snapshot importer (CRI + network hints + config map), (b) traffic emulator that supports multi‑tenant prefix/KV patterns and variable seq-length distributions, (c) metrics collector for tokens/sec, p95, p99, error rates, and per-route token-cost, (d) regression detector with configurable thresholds and a simple dashboard. Do not include full UI rollout in MVP—console integration will be a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can import a sanitized environment snapshot and instantiate an emulated topology in CI or a dedicated private sandbox
Run produces time‑series for tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, model throughput, and error rate aggregated by route
Automated comparison against a golden baseline with regression detection triggers when p95 increases by >15% or tokens/sec drops by >10%
Artifacts (logs, perf profiles, KV cache hits, and trace IDs) are archived to the benchmark store and linked in the run summary
Playbook for reproducing a customer perf report is documented with a working example run (Confluence link)
tasks: Design importer schema for environment snapshots (network groups, node types, GPU counts, quantization profile)
Implement traffic emulator supporting token-level distributions, correlated sequences, and tool/function call rates
Integrate Prometheus + tracing for metric collection and map metrics to run metadata
Build a small regression detection service (statistical diff + threshold rules) and alerting hook to Slack
Create CI job templates and a sample sanitized snapshot for solution engineers to run locally
Document runbook and add example customer case in Confluence with links to PRs and run artifacts
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting — aligned on MVP scope and marginal vs. catastrophic regression thresholds. Action: infra to reserve a private sandbox cluster (assigned to infra).
2026-02-24: Defined stable snapshot schema v0.1 and wireframe for how imports map to pod topology. Schema posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BI/Env+Snapshot+Schema

2026-03-02: Prototype traffic emulator done (branch: github.com/redwood/bench/orchestrator/proto). Supports per-route sequence distributions and KV cache priming. Initial local runs show 8k tokens/sec on a 4xA100 private cluster baseline.

2026-03-09: Observability hooks merged to feature branch. Prometheus metric names standardized: redwood_bench_tokens_per_sec, redwood_bench_latency_p95_ms, redwood_bench_kv_hit_ratio. Added run metadata labels for model_name and quantization_profile.

2026-03-12: First end-to-end emulation against sanitized customer snapshot (customer: AcmeCorp‑sanitized) produced a p95 of 215ms and tokens/sec 5.2k; baseline golden run recorded p95 180ms. Regression detector flagged p95 +19% (ticket routed to runtime perf team).

2026-03-14: Security review kickoff scheduled. Found that snapshots may contain sensitive hostnames — added mandatory sanitization step and SOPS-enforced secrets handling for snapshot artifacts (PR: github.com/redwood/bench/pulls/158).
comments: Marcus Nguyen (2026-03-05): Reviewed prototype. Suggest adding KV priming hook to reduce cold-start p95 variance. Filed subtask ENG-24625 to implement KV priming orchestration.

Lena Ortiz, Solutions Eng (2026-03-10): Ran orchestrator against a customer snapshot. Notes: network egress shaping had outsized impact on tokens/sec; recommend capturing egress rules in snapshot schema.
PR thread: github.com/redwood/bench/pulls/158 — please include unit tests for metric label propagation before merge.
PM note: Add a small matrix of model variants (float16, int8 quant) for each run to help triage quantization regressions.
risks: Snapshot sanitization may miss PII — required manual audit step for MVP
Network emulation fidelity versus actual customer networks may produce false positives/negatives for regressions
Resource cost of running private sandboxes for large customer snapshots—need quota guardrails
next_steps: Complete KV priming orchestration (ENG-24625) and land tests for metric label propagation
Finalize security review and implement SOPS snapshot encryption workflow
Create a follow-up PM ticket to scope Console integration for run visualization and historical baselines
